beats.text: Cole Harlan signs the motor-court card in a name that will not be checked and takes the key for the end room. He does not unpack. He puts the bag on the chair and goes to the window to look at the lot and the street beyond it.

He pulls the already-drawn curtains tighter on the rod. He takes a cheap spiral notebook from the bag and sets it open on the desk. He writes dusk and the time shown by the parking-lot lamps. He puts no date on the page.

From the window he counts the seconds between the bakery sign flicker and the church bell. He writes the interval in the first column. He counts the same gap again and writes the second figure beside the first without changing either.

His hands begin to shake on the pen. He stops counting the street and writes the tremor as a number under the intervals. He looks at the door and does not go out to hunt. He leaves the notebook open and sits on the made bed with his coat still on.

sc-001.dramatic_function: Inciting entry: Cole seals himself in and chooses measurement over hunt.

questions_opened.q01: Why does Cole time the streets instead of hunting?
questions_opened.q02: What constraint makes hunting the wrong first move?

beats.text: Anton Voss opens the tribute ledger on the Lodge blotter and rules a fresh night column before anyone new has found the door. He keeps the book square to the desk edge and does not look up when the hall clock marks the hour.

He restamps eight vials already in the tray and notes in the margin which will thin by the third dawn. He initials exclusive access against three host names already written in the book. He does not add a fourth.

A runner brings a folded cash-count and waits. Voss does not smile. He writes a number smaller than the one the runner named and slides the difference into the house column, the only order that has looked solvent to him since a prior book went to zero.

He leaves the ledger open on the blotter and sets the restamped vials back in their tray by decay order. He does not lock the office. He sits with the house column in front of him and waits for the first new name to come to the door.

sc-002.dramatic_function: Antagonist going concern: the tribute book is already the town's path to blood.

questions_opened.q04: Which hosts already have exclusive access stamped?

beats.text: Cole's hands have gone past a useful shake. Downtown doors that would have been free already carry marks. He follows the marks to the Lodge and stands in the office doorway until Voss looks up from the open book.

Voss names a price for a named hour with an unnamed clerk on the night shift and offers client terms that would put Cole on the page. Cole asks for the number again and refuses the bind, stating the hour is all he is buying.
Cole pays the hour in stamped value without sitting. Voss takes the payment and does not rewrite the offer. He nods toward the back office and keeps his pen on the side column.

In the back office Cole feeds from the clerk the way he would take a reading off a meter. He stops at the first number that lets him stand. He leaves her in the chair, breathing, and does not look at her face on the way out.
Voss writes paid-unbound in a side column and does not stand to watch Cole go. He leaves the terms offer on the blotter unaccepted and turns the page to the next open hour.

sc-003.dramatic_function: Price of admission: hunger forces a Lodge feed on unpaid-unbound terms.

beats.text: Maren Ellison wakes in the walk-up over the cassette shop and finds finger-marks on her upper arms. Last night's sleep should have taken them with the hours. She turns her arms under the bathroom light and counts the marks instead of washing them first.

She treats the marks as a wardrobe problem and lays out a long-sleeve shirt. Then she treats them as a work problem and writes the count of the bruises on a scrap by the sink. She does not call anyone.

Downstairs the cassette shop has opened for the late afternoon. She goes down in the long sleeves without locking the walk-up. She stands at the counter and checks the return bin the way she would on any work errand.

In the return bin a C90 carries her own handwriting on the spine. She takes it without asking the clerk whether anyone logged the return. She turns it over once and puts it in her pocket before anyone else can claim it.

She plays the tape on the counter deck. Her own voice from a night she cannot place counts a set list and then goes quiet in a way that is not a song. She stops the deck before the clerk can comment and takes the cassette upstairs.

sc-004.dramatic_function: Host rupture: bruises and a cassette make missing hours a work problem.

questions_opened.q07: Who left finger-marks sleep should have taken?

beats.text: Maren takes The Hollow stage in the long sleeves and sets her own levels. She treats the bruises as someone else's wardrobe error and starts the first song on time without looking at the back rail.

Cole leaves the Lodge and stands at The Hollow's back rail with the spiral notebook already open. He does not take a table. He does not send a drink to the stage. He writes the start time of the first song as a number.
The set is underway. Maren works the room as a shift. Cole times each song to the second, including the one the room already knows, and keeps a running column with no name at the top of the page.

When she looks past the lights toward the back rail he is already writing the next interval and does not lift his face. She holds the look a beat longer than the song needs and then turns back to the microphone.
She finishes the set without asking anyone to stay and leaves the stage by the side stairs. Cole closes the column. He still has not written a name at the top. He does not go to the merch table.

beats.text: The Hollow empties after last call. Maren's set is over and the stage lights go down. Cole puts the notebook away and leaves by the lot door before anyone can ask what he was timing.
He is back in the end room of the motor court before first light. He draws the curtains on their existing line and sleeps through the day with the notebook on the desk, still untitled.

He wakes on the second night hungrier than he was at the first dusk. He does not go out. He sits at the desk, opens the spiral to a clean page, and writes the seven-night remainder at the top as a fraction.
He rules four columns before he puts his coat on. Hunger. Sun-margin. Stored decay. Chapel window. He underlines the last dawn. He writes no name. The page is now a book of times.

He tests the curtain seam with a match and times how long he can stand the heat before the cloth would fail. He writes that number under sun-margin. He writes the commitment that follows: be first at that window, or the page is waste.

sc-006.dramatic_function: Goal lock: four columns and a first-at-the-window commitment.

beats.text: Cole leaves the motor court after dark and walks downtown with the notebook in his coat. He does not hunt. He watches a side-street bar reach last call and waits for the bartender to lock up alone.

He stops the closing bartender on the side street and does not feed. He leaves a marked coin and a time written on the back of a till receipt where the man will find them after sleep. He does not explain the objects.

He waits the rest of the night in a doorway, then holds through the thin day-edge in the motor-court dark. Hunger rises while he does not feed. After the next dusk he is back on the same side street in full night.

The coin is in the tip jar. The receipt is in the man's pocket. Asked what time he locked up, the bartender names the wrong hour and laughs it off as a long shift. Cole writes the loss where it can be seen.
Cole does not correct him. He lets the wrong hour stand and closes the notebook on the visible loss. He leaves the bartender with the coin and the receipt and no account of what was taken.

sc-007.dramatic_function: Recon test: sleep-erasure is proven where the loss can be seen.

questions_opened.q10: If objects survive sleep and the hour does not, what is a host's word worth?

beats.text: Cole walks the cemetery edge from downtown to the stone chapel. He keeps the notebook open and starts the first timing at the west door, then crosses to the memorial tower and times the same ground back.

He times the chapel against the memorial tower, door to door, in both directions, and writes the minutes. He marks the tower stair as a second approach that would still work in last light. He does not try the tower door from the inside.
The vestry hook holds a key that fits the main lock and is not alarmed. He pockets it. He writes the key as ordinary hardware and does not test it from the inside either.

Fog starts to thicken the intervals between the chapel and the tower. He closes the notebook on the two approaches and leaves the cemetery before the times go sloppy. The west door stays shut behind him.

sc-008.dramatic_function: Recon plant: chapel key and tower minutes enter the book as hardware.

beats.text: Cole takes a feed he does not need for himself on the way back from the cemetery, enough to stand and to pay with. He arrives at the Lodge with stamped value still on him and the notebook in his coat.
He has Voss write a line against the singer at The Hollow. He pays over a vial plus an amount that makes Voss look up from the blotter. Cole does not name what the surplus is for.

Voss records a credit in her name because that is how the book holds a surplus. He then treats the line as inventory he owns and does not say so. He initials the entry the way he initials exclusive access.

Cole folds the receipt into the timing notebook and writes her name in the street column as if it were an address. He files the line as Voss's claim on a mapped node. He does not ask what the extra bought.
Voss does not tell him. Cole leaves the office with the receipt in the notebook and no client stamp on his name. He does not go back to ask. He does not write the word owed anywhere on the page.

beats.text: Maren leaves The Hollow with the cassette in her coat and walks the campus night beat until she finds Deacon Ward at the usual checkpoint. She does not announce herself. She sets the tape on his clipboard as if it were another incident form and waits.

Deacon does not ask how she is or why she is on his route. He opens last night's incident book and reads the entries back as times, addresses, and what was left on the ground. He treats the tape as another object on the board rather than a request.

She stops him on a noise complaint logged behind The Hollow. The time on the page lands in the same minute her taped voice goes quiet. She holds the cassette against that line until the match is obvious. He reads the next entry as if she had not stopped him.

He offers to copy the page. She takes the copy and does not say please. He writes in the book that she took it, the same way he writes everything else, then closes the cover and returns to the route as if the exchange were finished.

sc-010.dramatic_function: Corroborating hand: Deacon reads the night as fact; Maren matches the tape to a timed complaint and takes a copy without asking.

beats.text: Maren walks back from the campus checkpoint to The Hollow with Deacon's copy in the same pocket as the cassette. The bar is still serving. She clocks in as if the night were ordinary work and heads for the stage before last call can empty the room.

She goes back on and keeps the house song in the set later than the room wants. A table near the door stops keeping time. The bartender checks the clock. She does not shorten the last change. She plays it again as if the room still owed her the bar.

Cole comes in from the Lodge with the timing notebook and takes a stool that gives him the room and the mic stand in one sightline. He starts counting intervals. He does not look at who has taken the next stool.

Lena Cho sits where she can see his notebook and Maren's hands on the stand. She does not introduce herself. She watches him count the room in intervals and miss the sleeve being used as a door. When he looks up she is already on the extra space in his margin.

She pays for her own drink and leaves before he can ask what she saw. He is still mid-count. The unread margin leaves with her. From the stage Maren sees only a woman stepping off a stool and not coming back.

After last call Maren plays the cassette through the stage monitor against the same changes. Phrases that were work-talk on the tape now sit on the bruises she can still see. She does not treat this as a haunting. She treats it as a second clock on the same night.

The bartender kills the lights while she is still at the monitor. She does not sleep. She writes the overlapping times on a set list, folds both papers into her coat, and stays on her feet in the dark as if sitting down would give the hours back.

sc-011.dramatic_function: Pattern and song, with a superior read in the room: the house song stops meaning the setlist; Lena files Cole's margin and leaves before he can ask.

beats.text: Night three starts at dusk. The Hollow is dark and the set is over. Guest hunger moves a notch on the clock whether anyone feeds or not. Voss is already in the Lodge office with the ledger open and a vial under the lamp.

He checks the vial against the lamp. The stamp is still sharp. The volume has already slid. He does not call anyone in to confirm the fade. He sets the vial back in the tray as if the number were still the number on the stamp.

He rules a new tax through the old one hard enough to cut the page. He tells no one it is because the stock is thinning. On a book that only honors what is stamped, the higher rate is the correct move.

He tells the room the house is tightening because unpaid hours make sloppy nights. He writes Pike's name in the enforcement column before Pike has come in, then underlines it once. His confidence in the dawn payout ticks down by the fade he will not name.

sc-012.dramatic_function: Tighten the tax: Voss raises tribute as stamped potency slides and writes Pike into the book before Pike arrives.

beats.text: Pike takes the name Voss underlined and walks it through downtown without hurrying. He does not call ahead. Shop lights are still on. He treats the route as a collection, not a chase, and the assignment is already hunting before the nonpayer knows the name has moved.

The nonpayer tries a side street, then a parked car, then the bakery alcove. Pike does not speech him and does not offer a revised rate. He only stays in the man's path until every indoor option is used up.

Pike backs the man into the sodium and denies him the next feed. The man breaks for open pavement and is gone from the match. Pike does not watch after the removal. He turns back toward the blocks that still have lights.
Shopkeepers lock early. The hour goes late on streets that have just seen a guest removed. Remaining guests now have one path to blood that will not bring Pike back out.

Voss, told by phone, marks the line paid-by-removal and does not leave the Lodge. He writes the tighter grip into the book as if a correctly run market had just proved itself. He does not ask Pike how it looked.

beats.text: Maren works the late set on night three as if the empty chairs were a timing problem. The house song is still in the book. She does not shorten it. She watches the door between numbers.

The usual after-show orbit fails to form. Two regulars who always stay for a pour take the side door instead. A man who has been too close for two nights now keeps the far wall and does not look at her hands.

She asks the bartender who paid her tab. He answers with a shrug that is also a closing and turns back to the glasses. The question that would have named the money dies on the bar. She does not ask twice.

She stays through the wipe-down anyway, awake on purpose. She writes the empty orbit on the back of Deacon's copy. She can feel money moving through a book she cannot see. She cannot read whose name the absence stands in.

sc-014.dramatic_function: Market shadow: Maren's after-show orbit empties; she feels money move and cannot read the line.

beats.text: Night four takes the streets back from the late hunt. Stamped potency slides another notch in the Lodge tray whether anyone opens a vial or not. Whitlock is still dark when Julian puts the key in the lock.

Julian Marek unlocks the house and starts the night by flattering the first arrivals for coming up the hill, then forgetting the compliment before they have their coats off. The party gathers around that small theft as if it were hospitality.

Cocaine lands on a silver tray beside the good whiskey. Hosts from campus are already in the side rooms. The door policy is hunger dressed as hospitality. Julian takes both, and his own hunger eases a notch.

Lena comes in without being walked. The climb and the night put a notch on her own clock. She does not wait to be announced. She stands where she can see which rooms he is offering and which he is about to take back.

Julian offers her the pretty downstairs salon and then gives it to someone louder. She takes the stairs instead and watches who he starves of a room on purpose. She files the withhold as a method, not as a slight.

sc-015.dramatic_function: Party opens: Julian unlocks Whitlock as a feed dressed as hospitality; Lena watches him starve rooms on purpose.

beats.text: Cole comes up the hill to time the house and takes the tray because refusing it would be a sentence. Drink and cocaine go down as measurements he will later have to correct. He is no longer sober when he clears the front hall.

Maren is already there. Julian brought the band and then parked them where the light is unkind. She takes what the tray offers because the house has already decided the night will not be held sober. The gap Cole had been measuring starts to close.

Julian walks Cole and Maren to an upstairs door, praises the lock, and then keeps the key on his own ring while he smiles as if he had given it. The party around them goes from gathering to peak on that withheld room.

The clock will not wait on dignity. Cole feeds in the wreck of the hallway, too near her, on a host who is not her. His hunger drops. The undeclared value in him rises by the feed. He does not look at her while he does it.
Morning has not yet collected. The night already has. Whatever working distance he had been keeping in columns is spent. He does not name what the nearness cost. He also does not put it back.

sc-016.dramatic_function: Forced proximity: cocaine, drink, and a withheld key wreck Cole's working distance from Maren; he feeds too near her.

beats.text: Lena follows Cole into the upstairs room Julian has already emptied of its promised privacy. She does not sit. She lets him have the ruined doorway at his back and stands where the extra column in his attention is visible.

She points at the way he has been watching the singer and asks who the surplus is for, as if asking for a time of day. She does not offer him a softer version of the question. She waits as if a number were the only decent reply.

Cole gives her a duration and then a first name. He then tries to make both of them back into street measurements, as if the name could be refiled as an interval. The concession is already out. He does not call it a debt.
She files the concession without thanking him. The read she has been building on him jumps: she now has the host, the surplus, and the place the map will fail. She spends none of that aloud.

She leaves him the room he did not want. She does not look back to see whether he will recode the name again. The question has already done its work. He is alone with a duration he cannot put back into the margin.

beats.text: The last hour empties the rooms into the halls. Bottles go over. Someone's coat is left on the stair. The peak noise breaks into smaller, meaner pieces. Julian still holds the door as if the house is his to close. The party is already a wreck and he is the last one treating it as a favor.

Julian walks a remaining guest out onto the drive to finish a cruelty he started in the hall. He withholds the last compliment the way he withheld the key. Cole is already in the portico shade, watching the gravel instead of the rooms. First grey is not yet on the stones.

First light takes the gravel in one pass. The drive is no longer shade. Downtown's hour goes with it. Julian looks at the margin the way he looked at a locked door and laughs. He does not come back in. Cole does not call him.

The sun does the rest in view of the upstairs windows. Julian's dawn margin hits zero on open gravel. His match ends there, unwritten. One fewer guest remains. Cole watches from the portico and does not move into the light.

Cole writes a rival removed. He does not write a tighter clock. Maren, aftermath-sick in a long sleeve, looks once at the drive and then at her own hands. The substances have become morning. Neither of them goes down to the gravel.

beats.text: Night five opens at the Lodge desk. Voss hears Julian's name as a gap in the book, not a eulogy. He does not ask how the drive looked. He asks who had been buying through those rooms.

He pulls Pike off the downtown hunt. The nonpayer is no longer the target. Pike comes in from the blocks and stands in the office while Voss writes Whitlock as a pickup, not a wake. The street hunt ends. Dusk owns downtown now.

Voss sends Pike to the Whitlock wreck and to every guest who had been buying through Julian's rooms. Unstamped vials come back in a box. Voss stamps them in his own hand. The count goes from eight to twelve. Potency is already sliding.

Named-host rights that were never written down get written now, in Voss's hand. Market grip tightens by the width of those new lines. He does not apologize to the empty drive. In a town that honors only what is stamped, the grab is the correct move.

He counts the twelve stamps and files the night as a book that will pay. His confidence climbs with the count. Somewhere off the book, Cole's hunger has moved with the missed hours. Voss does not price that. He prices what he can stamp.

beats.text: Night has taken the Whitlock drive back from the sun. The house stands empty. Cole is already back on the streets measuring a fire he has filed as a clearing. Maren has gone home sober. Lena lets herself into the motor-court end room.

The spiral is on the desk, face-up, columns clean. He left it here to measure a dead rival. She sits without turning on the lamp and reads the tower minutes and the unnamed surplus column the way she read his face in the emptied room.

She copies every interval into her own book, including the tower minutes and the surplus column. She files the copy as a hunt map to a second chapel entrance through the memorial tower, because that is the reading that pays. The original stays.

She spends the concession she already extracted: the name, the duration, the place his map will fail. Her read of him tightens by the width of the copy. She leaves the original a half-inch off its square, which is the only message she can afford.

beats.text: Lena uses the copied times to walk the memorial-tower stair in tonight's window instead of waiting for his. She does not leave a note that would let him catch up. She leaves him the half-inch on the desk. The inner door is still supposed to be shut.

The inner door gives on the minutes she copied. She marks how long it stays usable after first grey. The tower is a door now, not a landmark. She does not go through into the chapel. She only needs the lead.

She feeds once on the way back down so the stake in her coat is real. Hunger drops. The blood-value she can declare doubles. She wipes her mouth and does not look at the host's face long enough to owe anything.

The lead is a night he cannot recompute from lamps and hunger alone. She puts herself one night ahead of his analysis and keeps the minutes. She does not go back to the motor court. The half-inch is already the message.

sc-021.dramatic_function: Night taken: Lena walks the tower a night early and does not leave Cole a way to catch up.

beats.text: Cole comes back to the end room from the downtown blocks. The curtains are still drawn. He is measuring a death he already filed as a clearing. The desk looks wrong before he can say why.
He finds the spiral a half-inch off its square. He does not need a name to know someone read it. He takes it off the desk. The columns are still his handwriting. The square is not.

He flips the columns and times the gap against his own last mark. He cannot make the missing interval return. Analysis has already been spent. He does not go back to the tower. Going would only confirm a night he cannot buy back.

He closes the book face-down hard enough to bend the cover. He writes a number he already knows is late and sits with it until the shake in his hands is hunger again and not the page. He does not reopen it.

sc-022.dramatic_function: Stolen measure felt: Cole finds the half-inch and cannot recompute the lost night.

beats.text: Dusk of the sixth night. Cole forces the closed notebook open. He reads the surplus column against the Hollow set times and the sleep-test receipt still folded in the back. The intervals are not streets. He has been timing the wrong object.

The hours are the window in which a host can keep a night by not sleeping. He files the notebook again, this time as a clock on her erasure, not a hunt map. The route he meant to ride to the rite was never his.

He takes out Voss's receipt. The line is a credit standing in her name from his own extra payment. He had filed it as Voss's claim on her. It is his outlay, written in her name, uncollectable by the book he paid.

He writes the correction small, as if a smaller hand could keep it from costing the route. He has the line right now and cannot put it back. He still does not say the word. He closes the book on the correction and does not leave the room.

sc-023.dramatic_function: Wrong file: Cole re-reads the credit and the clock; analysis becomes a debt he still will not name.

beats.text: A noise complaint comes across the campus desk with a side-street address that already matches a time in Deacon's book. He does not treat it as a haunting. He treats it as a line. The complaint names no student he knows.

He writes the address again, slower, because that is how he keeps a night. The complaint names a debt collection after hours. The pocket book now carries the collection address. The incident flag on the beat is up.

He puts the pocket book in his coat and goes, because he wrote it down and because Maren is still walking around with a copy of his last page. He does not call her. He does not wait for a second complaint. Written is already an order.

beats.text: Pike leaves the Lodge for the collection address Voss wrote as a guest debt Cole let age. Downtown is late now. Deacon is already moving off campus toward the same stoop because the address is in his pocket book. Neither of them is the guest named on the line.

Pike finds him on the stoop and tells him to walk, offering it as a courtesy that is not a choice. The collection is on. Voss's enforcement is on. Deacon reads the complaint number back instead of moving, as if the number could protect the body that wrote it.
Pike hits him to move him. When the guest still is not there and the night is long, Pike feeds. It is not a fight. It is a convenience taken on the wrong body. Deacon stops moving.

The debt line can be closed. A named host is spent. One fewer body in town will hold a feed. Pike wipes his mouth on his cuff and leaves the body in the alley. He does not write Deacon's name. The book did not ask for it.

Cole is not on the stoop. The death still spends the last distance he had been keeping. A guest debt has closed on a host's life. Keeping Maren as a node after this would make him the market he came to measure.

sc-025.dramatic_function: Collection on the wrong body: Pike closes a guest debt on Deacon; a host is spent.

beats.text: Maren reaches the alley on the times she already had, not on a call. Pike is still in the mouth of it, assignment not yet finished. Deacon is not going to read anything back. She does not run. Running would make a second collection.

Pike is gone before she reaches the coat. She goes through the pockets with the same hands she uses on a cable and takes the pocket book before a passing car can make her stop. The pages leave the body. They are hers now.

Voss's enforcement is spent on a host it was not sent for. She does not close Deacon's eyes. She does not leave a note. She puts his pages with the cassette and walks without running, which is the only dignity left that will not draw a second collection.

sc-026.dramatic_function: Evidence seized: Maren takes Deacon's pages off him before anyone else can.

beats.text: Maren leaves the downtown blocks and climbs to the walk-up. She does not lie down. Dusk of the seventh night is already on the stair. She hangs the bag on the chair back and stands in the room as if sitting were a start of sleep.

She takes the cassette, Deacon's pocket book, and her own set-list times out of the bag and lays them in a line on the table. She turns the lamp up until the bruises show in the mirror over the sink. She looks at them as work, not as a wound.
Coffee goes on. Downstairs the cassette shop closes and the street noise thins. She presses play on the tape once more and listens standing, one hand on the table so she will not drift.
She stops the tape before her recorded voice goes quiet and leaves it cued. Sleep now would take the hours she has finally held. She will not give them back to the collector that lives in a bed.
She buttons the long sleeve over the marks so the street will not read them and sits in the chair facing the table. She stays there until dusk is used up. The night she kept is still hers.

sc-027.dramatic_function: Point of no return: Maren refuses sleep through the seventh night and lays the copies out as the only testimony the town cannot erase.

beats.text: Cole leaves the motor court with the chapel key in one pocket and the corrected notebook in the other. He does not go to Maren's door. He does not turn toward the Lodge. Downtown is still giving blood that has not been stamped.

He takes a first feed off an unnamed host in an alley off the square and stops at a number he has already chosen. The host slumps against brick. He does not check a pulse past the count and does not write the block down.

He feeds a second time two streets over and stops at the same kind of number. He carries what he took as undeclared value and leaves both hosts where they fall. Hunger is down to a working level. The stake he can speak is now enough.
Aftermath is out of him by the end of the second feed. He walks the downtown blocks counting the minutes to first light as a remaining fraction, not as a street, and does not look up at her window.

sc-028.dramatic_function: Stake gathered: Cole stockpiles undeclared blood-value on the last night, sobers, and keeps off both her door and the Lodge.

beats.text: First grey hits the cemetery wall. Cole walks the last blocks from downtown with the vestry key already in his hand. He does not run. Other feet are already on other approaches, too far off to name.
He puts the vestry key in the chapel main door and turns it. The lock is ordinary and it gives. The door stands keyed open on the first light. He does not push it wide.
He steps into the threshold with the undeclared value still on him and does not speak a stake. The last-dawn window is open. He is the first body the nave can count.
He keeps to the shade of the doorway and waits one measured breath for the window to be fully open. It is the last clean habit he has. He does not look back down the path.

sc-029.dramatic_function: Threshold: Cole unlocks the chapel main door at first light with enough undeclared blood-value to pay and does not yet speak.

beats.text: Voss comes up the chapel path from the Lodge with the ledger under his arm and the last stamped vials in a case that used to look like solvency. He does not hurry. The window is already open and he treats that as a desk hour.
He sets the ledger and the case on the rail as if the town were still a desk. The book and the vial case leave his hands. The case sits on the rail the way a deposit sits on a counter.
He nods at Cole the way a creditor nods at a man who paid unbound and then made a mess. He does not offer a term. He does not ask what Cole is doing in the doorway. The nod is the whole account.

He does not yet open a vial. When he lifts the case lid the stamps are still good and the blood has already gone thin. He opens the book to Maren's line and keeps his finger there, ready to read it as a stake the night has been trained to treat as his.

beats.text: Lena takes the memorial-tower stair on the minutes she already walked. She does not check the notebook copy. The inner door is still usable. First light is already on the stone of the landing.
She comes into the chapel from the memorial side with the stake in her coat. She does not look at Cole long enough to give him a rerun of the question. She does not look at Voss or the book.

She takes the place at the rail the tower door was always going to pay. First light is already on the nave floor. She has enough to speak and the lead to speak first. She waits only for the window to be used.
She stands at the rail with her hands empty and the stake still in the coat. She does not announce herself. The lead she spent a night to take is now a position, not a theory.

beats.text: Maren walks the cemetery path with the cassette, Deacon's pocket book, and the set-list times in one bag. She has not slept. The bruises are still on her under the long sleeve. She does not hurry and she does not hide the bag.

She comes to the keyed-open main door and stops in the threshold beside Cole because that is the light she can stand. She does not greet him. She does not ask if the room will have her. She takes the shade as a fact.

She does not offer the bag as a plea. She sets it on the stone as testimony in a place that has no court. The cassette leaves her hands and stays on the threshold where anyone who will look can see it.

She keeps her eyes open on the nave as if sleep were another collector. She does not look at the book on the rail. She does not look at the woman already standing there. The night she kept is in the bag and in the bruises.

beats.text: First light reaches the chapel threshold and widens on the stone. Cole has the key, the undeclared blood-value, and a clear path to speak the stake. Maren is beside him with the cassette and Deacon's pages, still awake. The nave is open.
He looks at the nave, then at her. He does not ask what she brought. He does not tell her the line in the book is a credit in her name. The look is the whole measure he has left.
He does not step forward to declare. He stays in the shade of the doorway as the light widens. The undeclared value stays on him and unsaid. He does not move his mouth toward a stake.
The door sits ajar on the widening light. The window remains open for anyone who will use it. He does not. His match ends here as a forfeit, not as an exit, and he remains in the shade with her.
He does not explain the choice to her. He does not apologize. She is still awake and he is still in the doorway, and that is the whole of what he will spend on this hour.

sc-033.dramatic_function: Refusal of the stake: in the doorway with Maren, Cole does not declare and stays in the shade while the window stays open for others.

beats.text: Lena speaks the stake from the tower side of the rail while Cole is still in the doorway not speaking. She names a blood-value and a completion, not a reason. She does not wait to see if he will change his mind.
The rite takes what she brought and does not ask who she was right about. The last-dawn window closes as a completed contract, not as a lapse. She is the completer. No second stake will be heard.
A mark that was never a person hands her the purse as a completed contract. She takes it. The match ends for her avatar alone. She is exited. The purse is no longer on the table.
She does not look back at the singer or at the book on the rail. She is gone from the chapel before the light has finished crossing the nave, with no one left inside to have been right about.

beats.text: Voss opens the ledger on the chapel rail and puts his hand on the last vials. He tries to read Maren's line as a stake in his name. The line will not spend. It is a credit standing in hers, and he is not her.
He breaks a vial. The stamp is good and the blood inside has gone thin as water. It will not stake. He tries a second and gets the same thin. His face does the math the book will not pay.
Remaining guests fall with the unpaid window. Pike, still somewhere downtown, goes with them. Voss's own match ends as a forfeit. He is still standing at the rail with a book that will not pay.

He closes the book on nothing and leaves the case where it is. The market was run correctly. Nothing in it is allowed to be declared. He does not look at Cole or at the singer when he steps off the rail.
